Chapter 6: Reclaiming Your Voice—Speaking Up and Being Heard
Picture this: there’s a quiet moment, maybe it’s as you’re driving alone, or sitting across from your therapist. Suddenly, it hits you—your own voice, the one inside, has been muffled for years. Not by accident, but by a lifetime of learning that every time you spoke up, it could mean ridicule, a cold shoulder, or being completely dismissed.
Have you ever wanted to share a thought—a feeling, or even something as simple as what you’d like for dinner—and been hit by a wave of anxiety? Maybe you’ve wondered, “What if I say the wrong thing? What if it upsets someone? What if nobody even hears me?”
For those who grew up with narcissistic mothers, that fear isn’t just in your head—it’s rooted in real memories. One woman remembers her mother always interrupting or talking over her at family gatherings. After a while, she just stopped sharing her opinions and nodded along, even when she disagreed.
Another person still feels the sting of being told she was “too sensitive” or “too dramatic” whenever she tried to express that she was hurt. The message was loud and clear: silence is safer.
But here’s something to pay attention to—the cost of silence is steep. When you keep swallowing your words, you start to feel invisible, like your thoughts and feelings don’t really matter. Relationships end up out of balance, with one person always accommodating and the other taking up all the space. After a while, you can lose sight of what you want—or even who you are.
Reclaiming your voice isn’t about picking fights or demanding attention. It’s about honoring your own experience, even when others don’t get it. It starts small. Maybe you share an opinion in a meeting. You say what you’d actually like for dinner. Or you tell a friend how you really feel about something. Each time you do, anxiety might show up, but so does a quiet sense of pride.
Most people don’t realize just how powerful those simple moments are. But over time, these small acts add up. They build your confidence. They remind you that your voice matters—not because someone else agrees, but because it’s yours.
So, if you’re on this journey, remember: every word spoken is a step toward wholeness. The path isn’t always easy, but your voice is worth reclaiming—one brave moment at a time.
